summary: A reader can ask the library to review an unavailable page from the terminal without identifying themselves to the desk.
realLife: Tacoma allowed patrons to send an access review request without supplying identifying information or a return email address. The plurality in the 2003 federal case described the government’s assurance that a patron need not justify an access request. Tacoma’s procedure separately addressed whether the reader supplied a name.
inGame: needs: local review procedure and contact requirements.

turns.what: Staff receive the page address without a personal explanation at the counter.

turns.pulledBy: The reader wants a direct response.
turns.what: Staff explain what contact information would be needed.
turns.writesBack: The reader decides whether to supply it.

turns.what: A trustee asks the director to distinguish two fields on the review form.
turns.pulledBy: The draft says patrons need not explain their interest but leaves the identification field ambiguous.
turns.writesBack: The minutes record separate decisions on contact information and reasons for the request.
